question: Should signed publisher following become a permanent OpenClaw core capability under the referenced RFC and stacked PR architecture, or should publisher discovery remain an external ClawHub/plugin concern?
rationale: This PR creates new core CLI, shared persisted state, remote-network behavior, and signature-authority policy; code review cannot choose that durable product and trust boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve the core RFC stack
options.body: Sponsor the core direction, define the required landing order and trust contract, and require upgrade plus live CLI proof before merging any slice.

options.title: Narrow the core seam
options.body: Keep only generic signed-feed or plugin API primitives in core and move publisher-follow lifecycle, policy, and storage to the owning marketplace integration.

options.title: Pause the feature stack
options.body: Close or park the stacked drafts until the RFC and producer implementation demonstrate a concrete supported user workflow.

recommendation.title: Approve the core RFC stack
recommendation.body: Sponsor the core direction, define the required landing order and trust contract, and require upgrade plus live CLI proof before merging any slice.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository policy routes new feature architecture and permanent core ownership decisions to the project owner.
